taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.note: By eye from the photos (observations 18973867, 4706451, 192934618, 184760982, 19983391, 111591905, 184599582, 253321042): a wiry, much-branched mound of thin culms, woody at the base, few tiny blades, and airy, widely spreading pinkish-purple panicles. The panicle's colour is set by hand (Hitchcock (1935) p. 380, 381: lemma purple; pinkish purple in the photos; sRGB 140, 80, 120 by eye), as no colour character applies to a spikelet and flower_colour, which the family's rule reads, is a flower's; its spikelets come from the order's rules.

traits.life_span.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: perennial; culms woody or persistent at base.

traits.woodiness.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: culms woody or persistent at base, numerous, wiry.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: culms 30 to 100 cm tall or more, widely spreading or ascending through bushes; most 30 cm to 80 cm.

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Muhlenbergia porteri: plants reach up to 3 feet (1 m) in height and are often highly branched.

traits.culm_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: culms 30 to 100 cm tall or more, mostly branching from all the nodes.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: FEIS species review, Muhlenbergia porteri: a drought-resistant, native perennial bunchgrass.

traits.clonal.note: FEIS species review, Muhlenbergia porteri: a bunchgrass; regenerates by seed.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: blades early deciduous from the sheaths.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: blades mostly about 1 mm wide, flat, 2 to 5 cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: blades mostly about 1 mm wide.

traits.inflorescence.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: panicle 5 to 10 cm long, open, the slender branches and branchlets brittle, widely spreading.

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Airy panicles held up at the culm tips, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 18973867, 4706451, 192934618, 184760982, 19983391, 111591905, 184599582, 253321042): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: panicle 5 to 10 cm long.

traits.florets_per_spikelet.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: one floret to a spikelet, as in every Muhlenbergia.

traits.glumes.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: glumes narrow, acuminate, slightly unequal, the second about 2 mm long.

traits.upper_glume_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: the second glume about 2 mm long.

traits.lemma_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: lemma purple, acuminate, sparsely pubescent, 3 to 4 mm long.

traits.spikelet_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: lemma 3 to 4 mm long, longer than the glumes: the spikelet as long.

traits.awns.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: lemma with a delicate awn about 5 to 8 mm long.

traits.awn_length_m.note: Hitchcock, Manual of the Grasses of the United States (1935) p. 380, 381, Muhlenbergia porteri: a delicate awn about 5 to 8 mm long.

traits.awn_insertion.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the awn leaves the lemma's acuminate tip.

traits.fruit_type.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: a grain (caryopsis), as in every grass.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles, Flowering Plants and Ferns of Arizona (1942) p. 119, Muhlenbergia porteri: mesas and rocky slopes, 1,800 to 5,000 feet, August to October. FEIS (northern Chihuahuan Desert, New Mexico): flowers April-May.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: grains ripe September to November.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for bush muhly from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.6 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m), batch s1b (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles, Hitchcock and Flora of North America, counts and colours from photos.
